content: Readwise Reader (power-reader benchmark) observed table-stakes library features: (1) Library (manually curated: Inbox/Later/Archive/Shortlist) + Feed (auto-pushed RSS) split; (2) Multiple save paths: browser extension, mobile share sheet, drag-drop upload, paste-URL; (3) Multi-format intake: PDF/EPUB/Markdown/OPML/HTML/RSS/email-newsletter/tweet/video/podcast; (4) Per-document metadata: url, tags, title, author, summary, category, image_url, site_name, document_note, saved/published/last_opened dates, reading-progress %, words, highlights count, minutes (reading time); (5) Edit metadata panel (Shift+M) - essential because PDF/Markdown metadata is 'often improperly set or not set at all'; (6) Exports: Library CSV, OPML feeds, full-content ZIP, Markdown highlights with Jinja2 template variables (url/tags/title/author/summary/category/image_url/site_name/document_note/highlights); (7) Per-document Notebook tab (annotation review surface, copy/export from there); (8) Manage Tags page split into Document Tags vs Highlight Tags with explicit 'no inheritance'; (9) De-dup by exact URL only - cannot detect content duplicates (utm params create second copy); (10) Immutability: saved article is never re-parsed to preserve highlight context - refresh requires delete + re-save; (11) Bulk Actions (Shift+B) for filtered lists.
